note: Open list. A record may name a region not listed here; validate.py warns so it can be added. Regions are the wine world's own geography, not administrative units.

entries.name: The world
entries.note: use when a node belongs everywhere pinot noir is grown

entries.name: Burgundy
entries.note: the Côte d'Or and its neighbours; the grape's home ground and its reference set

entries.note: Corton south to Santenay; reds and the great whites share the hill

entries.name: Côte Chalonnaise
entries.note: Rully, Mercurey, Givry — the same limestone, gentler prices

entries.name: Champagne
entries.note: pinot noir by area is the region's largest planting, mostly pressed white

entries.name: Alsace
entries.note: the one red grape the appellation allows

entries.name: Loire
entries.note: Sancerre rouge, Menetou-Salon, the northern edge of ripeness

entries.name: Jura
entries.note: Arbois and Côtes du Jura, often beside poulsard and trousseau

entries.name: Germany
entries.note: spätburgunder; the third-largest pinot noir planting on earth

entries.name: Ahr
entries.note: a narrow slate valley north of the Mosel that grows almost nothing else

entries.name: Baden
entries.note: the warmest German region, across the Rhine from Alsace

entries.name: Pfalz
entries.note: sandstone and limestone, riesling's neighbour

entries.name: Switzerland
entries.note: blauburgunder in Graubünden, pinot noir in Valais and Neuchâtel

entries.name: Alto Adige
entries.note: blauburgunder / pinot nero on the high terraces above Bolzano

entries.name: England
entries.note: chalk and sparkling wine; still reds where the season allows

entries.name: Oregon
entries.note: the Willamette Valley and the AVAs nested inside it

entries.name: Willamette Valley
entries.note: a hundred miles of valley floor and volcanic hills south of Portland

entries.name: California
entries.note: from Anderson Valley to the Santa Maria bench, wherever fog reaches

entries.name: Sonoma County
entries.note: Russian River, the true coast, Carneros' western half

entries.name: Russian River Valley
entries.note: fog up the river valley, and the AVA that taught California what pinot could do

entries.note: benchland terraces above the Salinas Valley wind

entries.name: New York
entries.note: the Finger Lakes and Long Island

entries.note: deep glacial lakes holding off the winter

entries.name: Central Otago
entries.note: the southernmost wine region on earth, and continental with it
